proof.text: Fix $j$. Define a simplicial set $T(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] whose $q$-simplices are strings $i_0\to\cdots\to i_q\to j$. For $f:[m]\to[q]$, retain vertices $i_{f(0)},\ldots,i_{f(m)}$, use the composite along the original string between successive retained vertices, and use the composite from $i_{f(m)}$ to $j$ as final arrow. An empty composite is an identity. Associativity and the identity laws show $T(f)T(g)=T(gf)$ for composable ordinal maps, and $T(1)=1$: both sides use precisely the same consecutive composites. For a surjection $f$, this is exactly the chain insertion in the statement, and $f(0)=0$, so it preserves the first vertex and its label object. All sets of strings are small because $I$ is small.

proof.text: A chain of $T(j)_q$ is degenerate exactly when one of its $q$ internal arrows is an identity. Indeed, if the arrow at $k<q$ is an identity, delete the repeated vertex and this identity to obtain a $(q-1)$-chain whose image under the surjection repeating $k$ is the original chain. Conversely, if $x=T(f)y$ for $f:[q]\to[m]$ with $m<q$, then $f$ is not injective. Monotonicity gives adjacent $k,k+1$ with $f(k)=f(k+1)$, and the corresponding arrow in $T(f)y$ is an empty composite, hence an identity. These are exactly the definition's degenerate simplices [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. The final arrow to $j$ is never an internal arrow and is not tested.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion to labelled chains and the colimit universal property of Tag 002F, categories.tex, definition-colimit.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], each $x\in T(j)_q$ has a unique normal form $x=T(\tau)z$ with $\tau:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $z$ nondegenerate. Step 2 shows that $z$ has no identity internal arrows. A surjection preserves the first vertex, so $x$ and $z$ have the same first vertex. If $x$ is degenerate, then $r<q$: otherwise $r=q$, the monotone surjection is the identity, and $x=z$ would be nondegenerate. Conversely $r<q$ makes $x$ degenerate by definition. In particular, for every degenerate $n$-chain its normal-form surjection is an object of $D_n$.

proof.text: Put $B_n(j)=\coprod_{x\in T(j)_n\text{ degenerate}}V(i_0(x))$, which exists by the assumed small coproducts. Write $e_y$ for the injection labelled by a chain $y$ into the relevant $S_aV(j)$, and $b_x$ for the injection into $B_n(j)$. For each $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $a<n$, define $k_\theta:S_aV(j)\to B_n(j)$ by $k_\theta e_y=b_{T(\theta)y}$; the source objects agree since $\theta(0)=0$. For an arrow $\theta\to\theta'$ represented by $\rho$ with $\theta=\rho\theta'$, we have $T(\theta')T(\rho)y=T(\theta)y$. Thus $k_{\theta'}S(\rho)=k_\theta$, tested on each coproduct injection. This is a cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion to labelled chains and the colimit universal property of Tag 002F, categories.tex, definition-colimit.

proof.text:
Take any cocone $(M,(c_\theta))$. For each degenerate $x\in T(j)_n$ with normal form $(r,\tau,z)$ from step 3, prescribe $h b_x=c_\tau e_z$, a map from the same object $V(i_0(x))$ to $M$. The coproduct property gives $h:B_n(j)\to M$. To check $h k_\theta=c_\theta$, take any $a$-chain $y$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to write $y=T(\rho)z$ with $\rho:[a]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $z$ nondegenerate. Then $T(\theta)y=T(\rho\theta)z$ is its unique normal form. Put $\tau=\rho\theta$; since $r\leq a<n$, $\tau\in D_n$, and $\rho$ represents an arrow $\tau\to\theta$. The cocone equation [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives
$$h k_\theta e_y=c_\tau e_z=c_\theta S(\rho)e_z=c_\theta e_y.$$
Every equality is an equality of morphisms out of $V(i_0(y))$; no element or image of an object of $\mathcal M$ is used.

proof.text: If $h'$ is another factorization, every degenerate $x$ has the normal form $(\tau,z)$ of step 3, and $b_x=k_\tau e_z$. Therefore $h'b_x=c_\tau e_z=hb_x$, and the coproduct property implies $h'=h$. Thus $(B_n(j),(k_\theta))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define $u:B_n(j)\to S_nV(j)$ by $ub_x=e_x$. Then $u k_\theta$ is the stipulated insertion map, on each injection $e_y$. Colimit uniqueness identifies any chosen $L_nS(j)$ canonically with $B_n(j)$ and its canonical map with $u$. This proves existence using only small coproducts, rather than assuming arbitrary colimits in $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion to labelled chains and the colimit universal property of Tag 002F, categories.tex, definition-colimit.

proof.text: Partition $T(j)_n$ into its degenerate and nondegenerate chains, characterized in step 2. The maps from $B_n(j)$ and $N_nV(j)$ to $S_nV(j)$ are given by $b_x\mapsto e_x$ and the corresponding injections for nondegenerate $x$. In the other direction, send $e_x$ to its injection into the appropriate one of these two coproducts, followed by its binary coproduct injection. Both composites are identities by their equations on every injection. This gives $S_nV(j)\cong B_n(j)\amalg N_nV(j)$ and then the asserted decomposition using step 6. For $n=0$ there is no proper surjection and no internal arrow, so $B_0(j)$ is the empty coproduct. Its unique map to each object proves it initial, exactly the empty-diagram colimit of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: For $v:j\to j'$, postcompose only the final arrow of each chain with $v$, retaining every internal arrow and the label object. For a natural transformation $\eta:V\to W$, retain the chain and use $\eta_{i_0}$ on its label. These operations preserve degenerate and nondegenerate indexing subsets and commute with all insertion maps: after each injection, both orders have the same chain and the same label morphism. They consequently define maps of the latching diagrams, of $B_n$ and $N_n$, and of the canonical cocones. The map on latching colimits is the unique one with these structure-map equations [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so the identification in step 6 commutes with both operations. The decomposition maps of step 7 also commute, checked on each injection. Identity and composition equations hold on injections too. This proves both requested naturalities, including $n=0$.

title: Nondegenerate-chain decomposition of the bar latching object
statement:
Let $I$ be a small category, let $\mathcal M$ be a category with all small coproducts, and let $V:I\to\mathcal M$ be a functor. Use the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ and $j\in I$, put
$$S_nV(j)=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j}V(i_0).$$
For an order-preserving surjection $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, the map $S_aV(j)\to S_nV(j)$ repeats the vertices according to $\theta$, inserts identity internal arrows, retains the final arrow to $j$, and acts identically on each $V(i_0)$-label. Let $D_n$ have objects the proper surjections $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, $a<n$. A morphism $\theta\to\theta'$ is a surjection $\rho:[a']\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ satisfying $\theta=\rho\theta'$. Give it the diagram $\theta\mapsto S_aV(j)$, with arrow map given by insertion according to $\rho$. Its canonical cocone to $S_nV(j)$ is the degree-$n$ simplicial latching cocone.
This diagram has a colimit $L_nS(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The canonical map to $S_nV(j)$ identifies, up to canonical isomorphism, with the coproduct injection
$$\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j\,;\,\exists k<n:\,(i_k\to i_{k+1})=1}V(i_0)\ \longrightarrow\ \coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j}V(i_0).$$
In particular there is a canonical decomposition
$$S_nV(j)\cong L_nS(j)\amalg N_nV(j),\qquad N_nV(j)=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j\,;\,\forall k<n:\,(i_k\to i_{k+1})\ne1}V(i_0).$$
Only the $n$ internal arrows are tested; the final arrow $i_n\to j$ may be an identity. These identifications commute with postcomposition in $j$ and natural transformations of $V$. For $n=0$, $D_n$ is empty and $L_0S(j)$ is initial. No model structure, cofibrancy, images, or monomorphism assumption on coproduct injections is required.
